subject: Weekly checkpoint: evaluation plan, data handling & deployment decisions
messages:
From: Elsa Monroe <elsa@finserv.io>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Dan Li <dan.li@finserv.io>, Procurement <procurement@finserv.io>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Week of May 18 checkpoint: data handling questions and timeline

Hi Monica / Neha,

Thanks for the quick turnaround last week. We want to lock the close timeline and get agreement on a few data-handling points before kicking the evaluation labs next Monday. High-level asks from our side: 

- Confirmation that the evaluation can run in a customer-controlled VPC (no egress to public internet)
- Clarify retention windows for test PII (masking vs synthetic) — our legal prefers 30 days max
- A short checklist for the evaluation plan so our infra team can provision ahead of time

Can we capture these in a short weekly checkpoint and assign owners? We have procurement constraints that require a signed MAP before we enable dedicated capacity.

Thanks — can join a quick call this afternoon if helpful.

Best,
Elsa
Elsa Monroe
Head of Integrations, FinServ Analytics
elsa@finserv.io

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Elsa Monroe <elsa@finserv.io>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 11:03:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Week of May 18 checkpoint: data handling questions and timeline

Hi Elsa — thanks for the clear list.

Short update and proposed owners / next steps: 

1) Deployment mode (VPC requirement) — Owner: Marcus Lin (SE)
   - We can run the evaluation in a customer VPC peered with Redwood Private (VPC peering or PrivateLink, depending on your cloud). Marcus will confirm network requirements and a minimal firewall/route table checklist.

2) PII handling & retention — Owner: Karthik Iyer (Security)
   - Recommendation: mask/obfuscate production identifiers before ingestion; if you must use real PII for functional tests we recommend a time-limited retention policy (30 days) and automated purge after validation. Karthik will provide the SOC2-relevant controls and evidence we can provide.

3) Evaluation plan checklist & infra prep — Owner: Neha Kapoor (AE)
   - Action: attach a short evaluation-checklist (attached) and the latest MAP spreadsheet. Please confirm: expected sustained throughput during eval (rps) and peak seq lengths so Marcus can size the nodes.

4) Close timeline / procurement — Owner: Monica Patel (AE)
   - Proposed close: target contract signature by 2026-06-04 if the MAP and procurement items are agreed. Monica to follow up with docs + draft DocuSign link.

Attachments: FinServ_MAP_v3.xlsx (MAP + milestones), evaluation-checklist.docx

Proposed next touch: 30-minute sync Mon 2026-05-25 10:00 PDT. If that works I'll send a calendar invite.

Cheers,
Monica
Monica Patel
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0189

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Elsa Monroe <elsa@finserv.io>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 24 May 2026 10:12:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Week of May 18 checkpoint: data handling questions and timeline

Adding technical details on the VPC/on-prem options (quick summary):

- Option A (preferred for fastest setup): PrivateLink endpoint into Redwood Private in your cloud account. Minimal routing changes, no public egress, supports dedicated inference nodes.
- Option B (on-prem or air-gapped): We can ship an on-prem bundle but it requires a 2–3 week ops window (installer, HSM/KMS integration if required).
- Network checklist (minimal): outbound to Redwood control plane only on TCP 443 to our control IP range (if using PrivateLink this is not required), inbound only from specified VPN/peers, subnets with /28 spare IPs for worker VMs.

Attachment: network-diagram_v1.png (high-level).

Marcus — I'll join the Monday sync to go through the diagram and sizing. Please reply with your expected rps and max token lengths.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Elsa Monroe <elsa@finserv.io>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 26 May 2026 14:30:02 -0700
Subject: Re: Week of May 18 checkpoint: data handling questions and timeline

Elsa / team — following up on PII and controls. Key points and proposed acceptance criteria for the eval: 

- PII definition: Redwood will treat fields labeled by FinServ as "PII" as sensitive. We request a mapping table (column name -> data type) prior to ingestion.
- Retention: 30 days max for real PII in evaluation, with automated purge job (we will provide purge log). If you use synthetic data we can mark retained data as non-PII and extend retention for analysis.
- Access controls: SE and Infra accounts will be limited; audit logs (read/write) will be exported to your S3 (or equivalent) daily.
- Evidence: I'll attach the SOC2 evidence checklist; if you need a tailored subset we can mark which controls are in scope for the short evaluation.

Open questions for FinServ: Do you need HSM-backed key storage for keys used in tokenization/encryption during the evaluation? If yes, we should flag this for procurement and shift the timeline by ~1 week.

Attachment: SOC2_evidence_list.pdf

I'll be on the Monday call to review acceptance criteria and confirm purge scripts.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

From: Elsa Monroe <elsa@finserv.io>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Dan Li <dan.li@finserv.io>, Procurement <procurement@finserv.io>
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 15:43:19 -0700
Subject: Re: Week of May 18 checkpoint: data handling questions and timeline

Thanks — this is really helpful. Quick answers and commitments from FinServ: 

- We'll provide the PII mapping table by EOD Monday (2026-05-31).
- We prefer PrivateLink if possible; HSM is not required for the evaluation but procurement may ask for optional language in the MAP.
- Expected eval load: 35 rps sustained, peaks ~120 rps; max seq length 8k tokens. Marcus, please confirm sizing for these numbers.
- Procurement: can you send the DocuSign draft and the short MAP milestone summary so our legal can review?

Agreed timeline: target signature by 2026-06-04. Procurement will fast-track if the DocuSign and MAP milestone spreadsheet are available this week.

Action items we captured on the call: 
- Monica: send DocuSign draft + MAP milestone one-pager (owner: Monica; due: 2026-05-29)
- Marcus: confirm node sizing & PrivateLink checklist (owner: Marcus; due: 2026-06-01)
- Karthik: provide purge script template and minimal SOC2 subset (owner: Karthik; due: 2026-05-31)
- FinServ: PII mapping table (owner: Elsa; due: 2026-05-31)

Please confirm or flag changes. If everything looks good I'll ask procurement to stand by for DocuSign.

Best,
Elsa
